extracted.intended_audience: journalism students and reporters covering political news and elections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journalists on how to cover political news and the specific kinds of election stories (analysis/forecast, day-of descriptions, and returns), plus standards on fairness and what to include in election-return summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of election stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Three common kinds of election stories are: (1) an analysis of political conditions preceding an election with or without a forecast of the result, (2) a description of election day conditions and events, (3) the results of the election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a distinct handling required for elections versus other political news; gives a canonical three-part typology for election coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of general political news
rubrics_metrics.description: Most political news falls into one of the general classes of stories already considered. Party conventions, campaign meetings, political speeches, interviews with candidates and party managers, for example, are treated like similar material in other fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implying that routine political events should be covered using the same news-writing conventions used for comparable non-political beats; only elections require a different handling (see 'Types of election stories').

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and separation of news and editorial
rubrics_metrics.description: Although some newspapers are sufficiently independent in politics to treat political news without partisan bias, many papers still present such news from the point of view of their editorial policy. There is a growing tendency, however, to present both sides fairly in news columns and to confine partisanship to editorials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States the normative standard for political reporting: strive to present both sides fairly in news copy and keep partisan viewpoint in the editorial pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of election-return stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Election return stories consist largely of summaries of the most important results of the election, such as: (1) the candidates elected and defeated, (2) the majority or plurality of the successful candidates, (3) the effect of the election on the political complexion of legislative bodies, (4) causes of victory and defeat, (5) statements by candidates and party managers in regard to the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist of key facts and angles when composing election-return summaries; emphasizes both quantitative returns (majorities/pluralities, bodies' composition) and qualitative analysis (causes, reactions).
